subject: Post-call: ops & scaling patterns for AtlasPay integration
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel@atlaspay.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 03 Nov 2027 15:24:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: ops & scaling patterns for AtlasPay integration

Thanks again for taking time today, Daniel — good conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps for the engineering deep-dive.

Summary of what we discussed:
- Integration surface: SDK + REST fallback, structured output for payment routing decisions, tool-calling for external KYC checks, embeddings for merchant lookup + reranker for disambiguation.
- Auth: customer JWT to Redwood gateway (mutual TLS optional for Private), per-route API keys for service-to-service.
- Routing: low-latency routing for authorizations vs async rerank/embeddings pipelines.
- Dedicated capacity needs: expected production SLA 99.95%, plan for reserved pool with burst capacity.

Immediate asks we left with you:
1) Peak QPS (per-region) and expected concurrency during payroll windows.
2) Typical prompt sizes / tokens for authorization vs lookup flows.
3) Any regulatory constraints that would require Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) or KMS/HSM.

Attachments: atlas_integration_diagram.png (high-level call flow), prelim_sizing.xlsx (template I filled with our rough numbers).

Proposed next steps:
- Can we schedule a 60–90m technical deep-dive next week (eng + infra) where we walk traffic patterns and run through the diagram? (Suggested slots: Tue/Thu mornings PST).
- If you can share a short traffic sample (CSV with timestamp, QPS, avg tokens) before the call, Sean and Olga can prepare a preliminary sizing and an autoscale/queue proposal.

Action owners:
- AtlasPay: Daniel — share QPS and tokens sample; copy procurement for SOW discussion.
- Redwood: Mina — coordinate schedule; Sean/Olga — prepare sizing & canary/fallback pattern.

Thanks — looking forward.

--
Mina Haddad
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks, Mina — solid recap. Confirming a few numbers from our side:
- Peak QPS (US-east): ~1,200 requests/sec during end-of-day clears; steady-state ~150 qps.
- Concurrency: peak concurrent active sessions ~340 (these are short auth calls, ~150-300 tokens).
- Embeddings/reranker flows are async for enrichment; those run at lower QPS (~40 qps) but larger token payloads (avg 1,200 tokens).
- We will need SOC 2 and a clear data retention policy; we expect Private deployment is likely required for our merchant PII.

I attached our procurement contact in case we need to accelerate SOW/terms. Happy to do Tue morning PT for the deep-dive — send time suggestions.

Thanks, Daniel — numbers are helpful. Couple of quick technical proposals before the deep-dive so we can be intentional with the sizing worksheet: 

High-level architecture options (trade-offs):
- Option A: Single unified endpoint for auth + rerank with dynamic routing inside Redwood (simpler SDK changes, higher peak GPU cost).
- Option B: Split path: low-latency auth endpoint (smaller model, aggressive batching disabled, per-request KV cache warm) + async embeddings/reranker worker pool (batched, larger kv cache, higher throughput).

Given your profile (1,200 peak qps; short auth tokens), we recommend Option B to preserve tail latency for authorizations. Initial sizing assumptions below are conservative (we'll refine with traffic traces):
- Auth path: 1,500 qps reserve (buffer for bursts), target p99 latency < 150ms, concurrency limit per instance 64, batch size 1–4 for tail latency-sensitive paths.
- Reranker/embeddings workers: pooled horizontally, batch size 32–128 depending on latency window; target throughput 300–600 tokens/sec per GPU for quantized model.
- Autoscale policy suggestion: scale auth pool based on queue depth + CPU/GPU utilization; scale embeddings pool on average batch wait time and SLO for enrichment completion.
- Queue depth recommendations: keepstanding auth queue depth shallow (<=500 requests) with aggressive shedding/fallbacks; allow deeper queues for enrichment (<=5,000) and use async callbacks.

Attachments: rb_inference_sizing_template.csv (I filled preliminary numbers aligned to Option B). Also linking a short doc with canary rollback patterns: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/atlaspay-integration-2027

Ask for AtlasPay: if you can dump ~24 hours of traffic (timestamped qps + tokens + percentile latencies) that would let us produce a tighter capacity plan.

I'll put time slots in the calendar for Tue 09:30–11:00 PT and Thu 09:00–10:30 PT; Mina, pick whichever works and I’ll set the invite with engineering leads.

--
Sean Gallagher
Principal Platform Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 04 Nov 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: ops & scaling patterns for AtlasPay integration

Couple of practical notes from the solutions side before the call: 

- Tokenization: auth prompts at ~150–300 tokens will be cheap CPU-wise but latency-sensitive; make sure SDKs default to short timeouts and prefer streaming + early stop where possible.
- Structured output/tool-calling: we should define a strict schema for routing decisions (JSON schema) and use Redwood's function-calling to map outputs into your downstream routing service. That reduces brittle NLP parsing.
- KV cache warm: for auth hot merchants, we can pre-warm KV entries to keep p99 latency tight.
- Canary/fallback runbook: propose warm canary (10% traffic) on dedicated pool + automatic fallback to hosted smaller model if dedicated pool is saturated. This avoids full outage during peak clears.
- Dedicated product note: reserved capacity supports burst pools (30% extra) for short windows; we can model that in the SOW so you don't overcommit.

I'll assemble a short runbook and a list of schema fields we want AtlasPay to confirm before the deep-dive (merchant id, routing priority, fraud flag enums, retention TTL). Mina — if you get the traffic sample from Daniel, I'll map it into the sizing template and return a draft SOW clause for reserved + burst pools.

Olga Petrov
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
olga_petrov@redwood.ai
